title: Route cargo through mr-boxington (mbx) for a shared compile cache
description: judgment wraps cargo with mbx via mise's wrappers key, pins it in mise.cloud.toml, caps its cache in the session-start hook and warms the build through it. Adapt the same for pact: mise.toml wrapper, cloud pin with checksum, hook cap/gc/warm, docs/development.md, and prove the mise run test legs still see the right target/debug/pact.
close_reason: mbx wraps cargo via mise.toml wrappers; cloud pin with checksum; hook installs the shim, sets the gc budget, warms through mbx; documented in docs/development.md#the-build-cache. Fresh-worktree all-features build 30s -> 11s.

title: Cloud sessions: a SessionStart hook that installs pact's development tools
acceptance_criteria: In a fresh cloud container, the first command of a session finds mise, shellcheck, cog, bd and pact on PATH, the beads database bootstrapped, and the build warm; the hook is idempotent and a no-op outside the cloud; mise run fmt-check, lint-scripts and a single test pass; docs/development.md says how it works.
close_reason: Done: .claude/hooks/session-start.sh (SessionStart, cloud only) with mise.cloud.toml installs mise, bd, cog and shellcheck from checksummed release URLs, updates rustup's stable to CI's, bootstraps beads and puts this checkout's pact on PATH. Measured here: first run 109 s, second 11 s, no-op outside the cloud; fmt-check, lint-scripts (now covering .claude/hooks/), check-docs and a single test pass.

title: Field run: one wave on real worktrunk, wt land side by side with pact merge
acceptance_criteria: pact audit over the run: every landed commit carries a Pact-Agent trailer and is covered; --check topology --expect worktrees reports no mismatch; no lease outlives its worktree; merge wait per landing route measured (mutex hold, compare-and-swap retries); findings recorded in docs/studies/worktrunk.md or docs/studies/field-runs.md.

title: commit-correlation reports a commit authored in the same second as its acquire as uncovered
description:
git author dates have whole-second resolution; hold bounds are nanosecond RFC 3339. src/audit/checks/commit_correlation.rs:310 tests `w.open <= c.at`. So a commit authored in the same second as its acquire, but after it, compares as earlier and is reported UNCOVERED COMMIT. This happens even when the same hold's recorded HEAD range already contains that exact commit, and the same report says the hold was "correlated by their recorded HEAD range".

Measured while writing the Reproduce block of docs/studies/worktrunk.md: acquire at 14:33:18.822, commit dated 14:33:18, finding, exit 1. Scripted or fast agents hit this, and the study's scenarios had to sleep a second after each acquire.

Possible fixes: compare at the resolution git records (floor the hold's open to the second), and/or count a commit inside the hold's own head range as covered, since that is a fact. Same check as pact-3ld (directory holds), different defect.
acceptance_criteria: A commit authored in the same second as its acquire, inside the hold's recorded range, is reported covered; a regression test pins it; commits genuinely before a hold still flag.
close_reason: Merged in #32: commit-correlation floors a hold's open to git's whole-second resolution.

title: A same-identity re-acquire from a different worktree is a silent refresh, though the worktree stamp tells it apart
description:
Two processes in two worktrees, both exporting PACT_AGENT=parent, both "acquire" the same file with exit 0 (measured). The lock is rewritten to name the second worktree while the first process still believes it holds the file.

That is the documented re-entrant refresh (src/lease/lifecycle.rs:580; docs/leases.md:932, "The trust boundary"). leases.md says its only trace is a renewed event "indistinguishable from genuine self-renewal" (:952). Across worktrees that is not true: the log reads `acquired … worktree proj.agent-a`, then `renewed … worktree proj.agent-b`.

A PID check was rejected because it misfires on an agent refreshing its own claim. But an agent refreshes from the worktree it works in, so a refresh that changes worktree is a different and deterministic signal. Refusing it does not bring back the PID check's false positives.

This matters next to worktrunk: its Claude Code plugin routes `isolation: "worktree"` subagents through `wt switch --create`, and a spawned agent inherits its parent's environment (fleet-patterns.md, "Declare what you launched"). The result is N subagents in N worktrees with one PACT_AGENT, which is a silent split-brain.
acceptance_criteria: Either lease acquire refuses (exit 2) a refresh whose lease is stamped with a different worktree, naming both worktrees and how to set a per-worktree identity, or pact audit reports it as a finding; leases.md's 'indistinguishable' sentence corrected; a test in tests/worktree.rs.
close_reason: Merged in #34: a same-identity acquire or renew from a different worktree is refused with exit 2.

title: pact init writes .gitattributes but leaves it out of its own commit
description:
src/cli/commands/init.rs writes .gitattributes (ensure_gitattributes: the merge=union rule for .pact/events.jsonl and .pact/messages.jsonl). But its commit's targets are only AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore and any instruction files (:207).

So a fresh `pact init` reports "committed 3 file(s)" and leaves `?? .gitattributes`. The comment just above that line says leaving a written file uncommitted "leaves a dirty tree it claims to have committed".

Consequence: the union merge rule exists only in that checkout's working tree, and clones and other checkouts merge the logs without it. No test asserts that .gitattributes is committed.

Found while setting up the experiments for docs/studies/worktrunk.md; not specific to worktrunk.

Edge case to decide: a pre-existing .gitattributes with unrelated uncommitted edits, which a path commit would sweep in.
acceptance_criteria: pact init commits .gitattributes alongside the other files it writes when it changed it; tests/cli.rs asserts a clean working tree after init in a fresh repository.
close_reason: Merged in #29: pact init now commits the .gitattributes it writes.

title: docs/audit.md's prepare-commit-msg hook double-signs commits rebased under another PACT_AGENT
description:
The hook at docs/audit.md:261 appends `Pact-Agent=$PACT_AGENT` to every message git builds, and `git rebase` builds one per replayed commit (measured with git 2.43). A branch rebased by anyone else gets a second trailer, e.g. `Pact-Agent: agent-b,orchestrator`. That includes an orchestrator, wt merge's rebase step, and `git pull --rebase` in a shared checkout. commit-correlation reads two different trailers as "cannot tell", by design.

Measured in docs/studies/worktrunk.md ("Landing, and what it does to the record"), --no-squash landing by the orchestrator:
- with the documented hook: 2 of 4 commits attributed;
- with `--if-exists doNothing` added: 4 of 4.

The case the hook was written for is unaffected: a first commit has no trailer yet, so the flag changes nothing there.
acceptance_criteria: docs/audit.md's hook reads: git interpret-trailers --in-place --if-exists doNothing --trailer "Pact-Agent=$PACT_AGENT" "$1", with one sentence on why; scripts/check-docs.sh green.
close_reason: Merged in #33: the audit.md trailer hook passes --if-exists doNothing.

title: --check topology reads a linked worktree named main (or outside) as the main checkout
description:
src/repo.rs:243 `invoked_from()` stamps every event with a linked worktree's own name, the literal "main" for the main checkout (:259), or "outside". A linked worktree whose name is literally `main` therefore gets the same stamp as the main checkout.

worktrunk's documented bare-repository layout (bare repo in <project>/.git, worktrees at <project>/<branch>) puts the default branch in exactly such a worktree. src/audit/checks/topology.rs:58 matches on the string. So an agent that did everything in linked worktrees fails `pact audit --check topology --expect worktrees` with `TOPOLOGY MISMATCH: 1 event(s) invoked from "main"`, and `--allow-main` would wrongly excuse it as the orchestrator. The event itself reads `worktree: "main", invoked_from: "main"`. A worktree named `outside` collides the same way.

Repro: the second block of docs/studies/worktrunk.md, "Reproduce".

Fix without reinterpreting committed rows: for example a separate field, or an escaped form only for linked names that collide with the reserved literals. Old rows must keep their meaning.
acceptance_criteria: An event written from a linked worktree named main or outside is distinguishable from the main checkout and from outside; --check topology classifies it as a worktree; logs written before the fix read exactly as before; tests/worktree.rs covers both names.
close_reason: Merged in #31: a linked worktree named main or outside is stamped worktree:main / worktree:outside.

title: worktrunk as the lifecycle layer for worktree fleets: follow-ups from the study
commit-correlation matches holds to commits by exact path, so a directory lease is never credited with commits under it
description: Found self-auditing a4c79aa: the hold on `.beads` (taken as the protocol block recommends, `pact lease acquire .beads/`) was reported as 'closed with no commit landing in their window' although that commit wrote .beads/issues.jsonl inside it, while the hold was live. src/audit/checks/commit_correlation.rs compares paths with equality (`paths.contains(&h.path)` at :209, `h.path == *path` at :296), never by prefix. Consequences: a directory hold always reads as read-only; a commit under a directory another agent holds is never a cross-held finding; and the uncovered-commit scope (paths leased at some point) misses files only ever leased through their directory. watch already has a prefix rule (watch::covers, with its documented src/render vs src/renderer.rs trap); reuse it rather than write a second one.
acceptance_criteria: a commit to dir/file inside a live hold on dir/ is credited to that hold; a peer's commit under it is cross-held; tests in commit_correlation.rs for both, and the src/render vs src/renderer.rs non-match

title: Record and grade the corpus on jev-1.13 (hosted) and tev1 (local Ollama)
description: jud record / eval / tune on the held-out split, both backends. tev1 decides whether the feature can keep messages on the machine: hosted means agent mail, which carries code, leaves it (see docs/telemetry.md's stance). Report accuracy with interval, ROC AUC, precision and recall at the tuned bar, and the drift between two identical runs.
acceptance_criteria: Numbers appended to docs/studies/system-one-triage.md; a go/no-go against the study's decision criteria (breaks_something recall >= 0.9 on held-out at a precision the operator accepts; tev1 within reach of jev to stay local)

title: Label a field-run mail corpus for the agent-mail rubric, two annotators, held-out split
description: The study's 33 messages come from one repository after the protocol restrained messaging, so only 4 are status reports, and the rubric was written after reading them. Export authored mail (kind=mail) from the field-run repositories (arkanoid, megablast, grimcast, crucible, quern) and the dogfooding run that sent 85 messages, 41 of them status pings. Label needs_action / breaks_something / status_only per the rubric's criteria, with a second annotator on at least a third.
acceptance_criteria: 150+ labelled messages as a jud Cases document; inter-annotator agreement reported per question; a held-out split fixed before any re-tuning

title: Decide whether PACT_BUILD_TIME should stop defeating the mbx cache for the pact crate
description: build.rs stamps chrono::Utc::now() into PACT_BUILD_TIME, so every build of the pact crate has a new compiler input: mbx reports 'incremental state was not reused: compiler environment input changed: PACT_BUILD_TIME' and only the dependencies are cached. Options: keep (provenance wins); stamp the commit time (git log -1 --format=%cI) plus -dirty, which is stable per commit but no longer says when a dirty build was made; or honour SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. Changes what pact --version prints, which is why it needs a decision rather than a drive-by. Measure the leaf-crate share of a warm worktree build (11 s total today) before choosing.
close_reason: Measured, keep the stamp. Fresh-worktree all-features test build ~11s in all four combinations of {per-build stamp, pinned stamp} x {MBX_SHARE_WORKSPACE_ROOT unset, 1}. Within a checkout the stamp costs only the first rebuild (8.0s vs 1.4s), then mbx's learned incremental brings edits to ~1.5s. The pact crate misses across worktrees because its source path differs (--remap-path-prefix), not because of the stamp. docs/development.md#the-build-cache corrected.

title: Upstream to worktrunk: .pact/ and .beads/ as built-in copy-ignored excludes; keep trailers through a squash
description:
Two asks for max-sixty/worktrunk. A human has to open them: the study's session had read-only access.

1. Add .pact/ and .beads/ to BUILTIN_COPY_IGNORED_EXCLUDES (src/commands/step/shared.rs at 057037a). That list already excludes tool-state directories (.conductor/, .entire/, .worktrees/) because tool state "shouldn't be shared between worktrees", and both directories fit that rationale exactly. The exclusion only affects ignored files: tracked files are never copied.

2. Carry the squashed commits' trailers (deduplicated) into the message `wt step squash` / `wt merge` builds. Today the message is new (an LLM's, or "Squash commits from <branch>" plus the subjects), so Pact-Agent and Co-Authored-By do not survive. GitHub's own squash merge keeps Co-authored-by.
acceptance_criteria: Issues or PRs opened on max-sixty/worktrunk with their links recorded here, or a recorded decision not to.

title: Design spike: a baseline-aware verify verdict a pre-merge hook can call
acceptance_criteria: A written design, or a recorded decision not to build one: the interface, where the baseline runs, and how it shares code with src/merge.rs. No implementation required.

title: doctor: warn when a linked worktree carries its own .pact/ runtime files or a .beads/ database
description:
`wt step copy-ignored`, worktrunk's recommended post-start hook for warm builds, copies every gitignored file from the primary worktree. Neither .pact/ nor .beads/ is on its built-in exclude list.

Measured in docs/studies/worktrunk.md: a live .pact/leases/*.lock, .pact/watches.jsonl, .pact/activity/* and bd's .beads/dolt/ store all landed in each new worktree.

Under the default shared scope pact ignores the copy. Under PACT_WORKTREE_SCOPE=local, or the per-worktree fallback a broken .git file triggers, the copy is the state: `lease ls` showed a released lease as active, and acquire refused with exit 2. bd's worktree guide calls a worktree's "own accidental .beads directory" a fault. pact doctor reported neither.

Proposed check, filesystem only (no bd call; beads.rs's runner stays private), run from a linked worktree: .pact/leases/ or .pact/watches.jsonl under the worktree's own root, or .beads/dolt / .beads/embeddeddolt there.
acceptance_criteria: doctor warns (never fails) from a linked worktree holding copied pact runtime state or a bd database, naming the paths and the likely cause; the new check name appears in docs/tui.md's Doctor list (check-docs.sh enforces it); a test in tests/worktree.rs.
close_reason: Merged in #30: pact doctor warns when a linked worktree carries copied .pact/ runtime state or a .beads/ database.

title: Move the worktrunk composition into fleet-patterns.md once the field run is clean
description:
The study's "How it should be wired" section is a proposal until a real run validates it. It covers the spawn line, the .config/wt.toml, approval hygiene, and the table for choosing between pact merge and wt land. The decision criterion in docs/studies/worktrunk.md: move it into docs/fleet-patterns.md once one wave on real worktrunk audits clean.

Per the docs placement rule, the how goes to fleet-patterns.md (the orchestrators' page) carrying the field run's numbers, and the study keeps the evidence. Use the docs-curator agent.
acceptance_criteria: docs/fleet-patterns.md carries the composition with the field run's numbers; the study links to it; scripts/check-docs.sh green.

title: Bare-repository layouts: the committed logs live outside every checkout, yet doctor calls them committable
description:
In both bare-repository layouts the shared state is outside every checkout:
- `<common>/pact/` for a bare repo named like `repo.git`;
- `<project>/.pact/` when the bare repo sits in a directory named `.git`, the layout worktrunk documents (tips-patterns, "Bare repository layout").

So .pact/events.jsonl and .pact/messages.jsonl can never be committed, and architecture.md calls these the only things pact stores that it cannot derive. doctor still reports `event log survives a clone: .pact/events.jsonl is not ignored and not yet committed — commit it and it travels`. The reason: clone_reach_check (src/doctor.rs:96, :106, :1125) runs repo::reach against the invoking checkout's root, not the state dir.

Separately, the <project>/.git case is reported as `state placement: main-worktree — the main worktree at <project>`, and <project> is not a worktree. architecture.md:436 calls this layout "pathological, and not worth code to detect", but worktrunk documents it as one where "no branch gets special treatment".

Coordination itself works in both layouts (measured: exit 2 across worktrees). The defect is the history and the diagnosis.
acceptance_criteria: From any worktree of either bare layout, doctor says the event log and message store cannot be committed from any checkout and names the decided remedy (a documented home for them); a bare repository in <project>/.git is reported as bare, not main-worktree; architecture.md's known-limits text updated; tests cover both bare shapes.

title: pact audit: calibration line for handoff --confidence (model-free)
description: handoff --confidence high|medium|low is self-reported and never measured. Relate each tier to an outcome pact can derive (a later commit fixing the same paths within N hours, or the dependent bead reopened) and report the rate per tier. A count, never a verdict, like the handoff-coverage line. Needs no model and no judgment dependency.
acceptance_criteria: audit prints per-tier outcome rates with counts; --json carries them; no check fails on it

title: Document the composition recipe: pact msg --json piped to jud, outside pact
description: If the corpus run says go: a fleet-patterns section (or docs/mcp.md, for an MCP triage agent) showing the read-side recipe with no code in pact. Ranks and escalates; never filters. Names the egress trade-off.
acceptance_criteria: Recipe runs end to end on a fixture inbox; check-docs green

title: System One triage of agent mail: follow-ups from the study
description: Follow-ups from docs/studies/system-one-triage.md. The study found one place a calibrated verdict helps pact: ranking authored mail by what it needs from its reader (needs_action, breaks_something, status_only), read side only, never hiding a message. Measured on pact's own 33 messages against jev-1.13.0: ranks well (ROC AUC 0.89-0.97), thresholds badly at 0.5. Everything here is gated on a larger labelled corpus.

title: commit-correlation: credit a squash commit to the hold whose range has the same patch-id
description:
Measured in docs/studies/worktrunk.md: wt merge's default squash, run by the orchestrator after release, lands 0 of 2 commits attributed and produces two UNCOVERED COMMIT findings (audit exit 1), for a fleet that followed the protocol exactly. The squash replaces who (the trailers are dropped) and when (the author date becomes the squash time). The study recommends `wt merge --no-commit`, which keeps 4 of 4.

If a fleet lands by squash anyway, commit-correlation could recognise a squash commit whose diff equals a recorded hold range's combined diff and credit it to that hold. That is `git patch-id` over <open-head>..<close-head>, the same fact worktrunk's own integration check uses, so it is a fact rather than a guess.

Defer until a fleet needs it.
acceptance_criteria: Only if pursued: a squash commit whose patch-id equals a hold range's is reported covered and attributed to that hold's agent; unrelated squashes still flag; tests use a real squash.

title: Design spike: optional judge feature for pact ui / doctor (rank, and alarm on unread warnings)
description: Only after the corpus run proves value. Constraints the study set: no default feature; never on msg inbox's hot path uncached; never sets an exit code or gates a command; never hides a message; verdicts cached by message id (content-derived, so stable) and reproducible from recordings; link judgment with --no-default-features and a blocking transport (the otel precedent) rather than shelling out to jud (the bd lesson). doctor alarm = verdict AND recorded fact (unread for N minutes), the fleet-liveness shape.
acceptance_criteria: A decision record: build it or not, with the dependency and binary-size cost measured
